scope.chapter: Normal Modal Logic — Syntax and Semantics

findings.finding: The biconditional substitution clause is guarded by prvIf, duplicating the conditional case, although its displayed operator and output both use liff.
findings.controlling_evidence: The frozen basic-language definition guards biconditional formation by prvIff and conditional formation by prvIf. The adjacent substitution clauses otherwise use matching tags and operators.
findings.required_translation_handling: Guard only the biconditional clause by prvIff; leave its formula unchanged and disclose the tag repair adjacent to that clause.

findings.finding: The box substitution clause is an unconditional list item, unlike the diamond clause and the frozen language definition where the box operator is guarded by prvBox.
findings.controlling_evidence: The frozen basic-language definition includes box formulas only under prvBox. This is a tag-scope repair for language variants, not a change to the recursive substitution formula.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use a prvBox tag item for the same box clause and disclose the scope repair next to it.

findings.finding: The first non-satisfaction expression for Box not A in the second duality argument omits [w], unlike the expression immediately to its left and its next occurrence.
findings.controlling_evidence: Every claim in this argument concerns truth at the same world w; the adjacent expressions explicitly supply [w], and the world-indexed satisfaction relation is defined in this chapter.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add [w] only to that first non-satisfaction expression and disclose the notation repair adjacent to the proof step.
